history.name: An agent never has to open the record
history.description: A mature ledger is a large body of text, and an agent that reads all of it to change one line pays for that on every edit and tends to reformat what it hands back. Everything is reachable instead through the reading commands — the index of the record, then the single entry about to be touched — so an edit costs a fraction of that and the record's shape stays under the tool's control rather than the agent's.
history.dev_notes: The design brief behind src/commands/read.mjs and the one-file-per-feature layout: the agent never reads the corpus and never writes JSON by hand.
